 253·9= Douglas Hyde (1860-1949), Irish scholar and translator.
 253.10: in Greek mythology, the nine Muses are the patrons of arts and sciences.
 253.11: according to his account in Autobiographies, the "one" is Yeats.
 253.13: John Millington Synge (1871-1909), Irish playwright.
 253.14: John Shawe-Taylor (1866-1911), active in the land reform movement;
Hugh Lane (1875-1915), art collector and critic. Both were nephews of Lady
Gregory.
 254: Coole Park is the estate of Lady Gregory in County Galway; for Thoor
Ballylee, see Yeats's note on "The Tower", pp. 459-6o.
 254.1-7: Yeats mistakenly suggests that the river which runs past Thoor Ballylee
flows into Coole Lake. The Irish poet Raftery (1784-1835), who was blind (thus
"dark"), described a deep pool in the river near Thoor Bally lee as the "cellar."
